records.name: Ribe
records.finding: The study compares adult age-at-death patterns across Viking, medieval, and post-medieval cemetery samples.
records.limitations: 943 is the combined sample, not the Viking-only denominator. Adult skeletal mean age at death is not life expectancy at birth. Burial selection, age estimation, and changing population structure matter.
records.comparison: A diachronic adult mortality sample; useful for period comparisons within the study, not a universal Viking lifespan.

records.name: Birka — grave Bj 581
records.finding: Genomics supported a female sex estimate for the person in grave Bj 581; the burial contained martial equipment.
records.limitations: The study reports no pathological or traumatic injuries. Genomic sex and the interpretation of a social role do not establish whether an individual fought in battle. One burial supplies no population prevalence.
records.comparison: An individual burial study. Its biological and contextual questions differ from a cemetery mortality distribution.

records.name: Varnhem
records.finding: 83 of 171 individuals had caries (49%). Among the permanent dentitions, 424 of 3,293 examined teeth were affected (13%).
records.limitations: The excavation and jaw-preservation criteria select the sample. These are different denominators, and the cemetery extends beyond the conventional Viking Age. Tooth loss can bias observed caries prevalence.
records.comparison: A dental disease study with explicit individual and tooth denominators. It does not measure general mortality.

records.name: L’Anse aux Meadows
records.sample_unit: worked wood pieces used for exact dating
records.finding: A cosmic-ray radiocarbon marker places the cutting of the studied wood in AD 1021.
records.limitations: These are wood samples, not human remains. The date documents activity at the site; it does not establish a disease introduction or a complete occupation interval.
records.comparison: Evidence of presence and chronology, without a skeletal health denominator.

records.name: Eastern Settlement, Greenland
records.sample_unit: No human skeletal sample in this model
records.finding: A sea-level model evaluates coastal flooding as a possible contributor to later Norse settlement abandonment.
records.limitations: The geographic marker locates the settlement region, not a sampled patient or exact model cell. Environmental pressure, epidemic mortality, and a sole cause of abandonment are separate claims.
records.comparison: Environmental modeling concerns a later Norse setting and cannot be pooled with Viking Age health samples.

records.name: Ridgeway Hill, Weymouth
records.date: Viking Age; see dating discussion in excavation report
records.sample_unit: Minimum number depends on the skeletal inventory; consult the report
records.finding: An excavated mass burial documents decapitation and a highly selected episode of violent death.
records.limitations: A mass execution is not a representative cemetery sample. The identity of the group and historical event attribution require separate arguments.
records.comparison: A mortality assemblage selected by violence; unsuitable for estimating routine population survival.
